chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

After the end of the world and the birth of a new, the first thing Phainon does is take a bath. He kind of deserves it after saving the planet, okay. 

...The second thing he does is visit a library.

Phainon walks through the halls of Castrum Kremnos, catches sight of a crowd of faces filled for once with hope, renewal. The citizens of Kremnos are starting to rebuild, shoving rubble aside and beginning anew. 

Phainon smiles, Mydei would love to see this sight. All the last king of Kremnos ever wanted for his people was to give them a fresh start. Perhaps Phainon will have to convey the success of such wishes when next he sees Mydeimos. He is the Deliverer, after all. It'll be nice to be the bearer of something good, something kind, for once.

After asking a local or two for directions, he finally finds himself at two large stone front doors. This marks Phainon’s first time in the famous Garbaniphoro Grand Library of Castrum Kremnos. 

As he wanders in, Phainon notes with a wistful sigh that it, too, is in disarray and debris. It's not yet been restored to what he’d imagined to be its former glory after bearing witness to the end of the world, and almost all shelves remain barren or covered in tattered and torn pages. 

Phainon treads carefully through the lined aisles, hand tracing along the shelf banisters. Dust lines his finger, but he doesn't wipe it off.

He turns each corner unhurriedly. After all, now, he has all the time in the world.

After a few minutes’ search, Phainon finds what he seeks, lips lifting and eyes settling at the corners.

There, in a nook hidden away between towering bookshelves, sits a man, with blond hair and red scars. A tome is balanced in his lap, and a pair of horn-rimmed reading glasses adorn his nose.

I found you, his heart whispers. 

For a moment, Phainon just stares, standing, frozen. After all this time, after all of the deaths and battles and losses and victories. After all of their sacrifices. There he is.

Mydei sits on a chair, calm and peaceful, and Phainon feels his heart strangling his throat.

There's so much he wants to say.

Stayed alive after all, Guardian?

It's been a while, hasn't it?

Your reading glasses make you look like a nerd.

I thought I'd never see you again.

...I missed you.

Phainon says,

“Not quite the next life, but here I am, visiting your library. So, will you teach me that language of yours?"

At his words, Mydei looks up, focus shifting to the source of the sound.

Most people didn't know this about Mydei, but, despite all his war cries and speeches fit for kings, he is actually a quiet man by nature. Prone to bouts of peace whenever he could borrow a moment to himself. Something in Phainon's chest settles to see that hasn't changed, that the black tide hasn't left Mydei a man morphed beyond recognition.

Mydei sets the tome on an adjacent table. There's nothing loud about his reaction, and yet—

“...HKS, we haven't seen each other since I left to fight the black tide, and that's the first drivel that comes out of your mouth?”

…the sound detonates in Phainon's heart, all the same.

Mydei's voice has that same roughness and rasp that he remembers, perhaps made moreso with disuse. Phainon's eyes fill with tears threatening to overflow.

…He's missed Mydei so fucking much.

“...Well, will you? I'm still waiting to know if your language has more than a couple words at all, really,” he says, going for teasing in his tone, but missing a step, landing on soft, sincere. He approaches Mydei with slow steps.

Mydei rises from his chair, rolls his eyes. “Fine, Deliverer.” With the same lethal speed he uses to dispatch his enemies, Mydei wraps his arms around Phainon’s back and squeezes him tight. The tears Phainon's been valiantly holding back start to fall and fall and fall.

He cries for a while, and Mydei just holds him closer, rubbing reassuring circles into his back and shoulders. Phainon clutches him back with all he has.

“... I'm glad you're alive,” Mydei says, quiet, steady. He's always been strong like that.

Phainon buries his face further into Mydei's embrace, whispers into his shoulder, “And I, you.”

In comparison to 10 days and 10 nights, this moment is likely child's play, a whisp on the fabric of time. Still, it feels like it stretches on forever, and time slows to a standstill where the only thing Phainon can hear is the sound of both of their hearts, beating, alive.

Then, after a good while has passed and all tears have run dry, Phainon is hit by a wave of embarrassment.

He steps back. “So ah… um, haha,” Phainon brings his right hand to rub the back of his neck, “That was awkward of me, huh?”

Mydei just raises an eyebrow as if to say when are you not?

Phainon generously ignores this slight and says, looking Mydei’s form up and down for injuries, “How have you been, Mydei?” 

“Dying a few thousand times or so. You know, that sort of thing,” Mydei says, deadpan.

Phainon stares at Mydei for a moment, eyes wide as it hits him, really hits him, that Mydei is here and real in his arms. Then, he bursts into laughter. Anyone who doesn't think Mydei has a sense of humor clearly hasn't spent enough time getting to know him.

The corners of Mydei's mouth lift into a grin, letting out a chuckle. He shifts his arm to curl around Phainon’s shoulders, bumping their sides together, playful, kind. “There's that laugh I know so well.”

Phainon sobers, aftereffects of laughter still shaking his sides. 

He loves this stupid man so fucking much.

Phainon uses their linked arms to bump Mydei back as they walk towards the library’s exit together. “Right back at you.”

The sun is shining bright and warm through the library windows, and perhaps everything will be alright.

—

“...And then, his dramatic ass decided not to meet me at the entrance gates to Castrum Kremnos, like a good host would, oh no , he has to sit in his decrepit old library looking all smug and waiting for me to find him!” Phainon complains, smashing his ale cup to the pub table, liquid sloshing out the edges.

Castorice sighs, “We know, Phainon. This is the third time you've told us this story already.”

Phainon plants his face into the table, groaning in defeat. “He really made me worried that something happened to him, but he was just taunting me the whole time!”

Mydei just sits with his arms crossed, looking pleased with himself. “Aw, you were worried about me, Deliverer?”

Phainon, face still kissing the tabletop, raises one hand in the air and swats it back and forth as if to smack Mydei, “Shut up, HKS.”

“...HKS?” Anaxa starts, head tilted in confusion. He has no drink of his own, but he's fooling no one sneaking more than a few sips of Aglaea’s.

“It's one of the very few words in the Kremnoan language, probably,” Phainon pouts, “means something like dumbass or weak or something.” His face is still glued to the table but Mydei can hear that pout in his voice.

“You know Kremnoan, Phainon?” Aglaea says in mild surprise, setting down her wine delicately, on the side opposite where Anaxa sits to her right.

“No I don't , because he won't teach meeeee,” Phainon whines into the table.

“...You were serious about learning it?” Mydei asks, voice soft for a beat. Then, tauntingly, “I thought you were just trying to play it cool for our reunion, MKN. Not that it worked, since you sobbed all over my shoulder right after.”

“Mekae- what?” Phainon says, confused, still planted into the tabletop and graciously ignoring the second part of what Mydei said.

For the first time that night, a faint blush starts to trace Mydei's cheeks. He huffs and looks away. “Nothing. It means you're a loser.”

“Is the Kremnoan language only made up of insults??” Phainon laments despairingly.

Tribbe says gleefully, “I don't know what that word Mydei said means, but I don't think it means what he said!”

“Shut up and drink your grape juice,” Mydei grumbles.

Hyacine giggles, hiding her mirth beneath her palm. It's really lovely to get to share this time with everyone again, without the threat of the end of the world on their shoulders.

—

Night now once again sets properly in Okhema, and it lasts until the Waking Hour. It's still dark out when Phainon jolts awake to an increasingly loud banging on his door.

“...What the hell?” he mumbles, staggering to the entrance.

“Open up, Deliverer!” Mydei commands from the other side of the door. Once a king, always a king, Phainon smiles to himself.

Phainon yanks open the door, “Someone better be fucking dying if you're waking me up this early,” he grumbles.

If his heart is singing in his chest and his eyes are softened at the edges at the sight of Mydei—who happens to be carrying a stack of books almost as tall as he is for some reason—the new sky-dark and her shadows will keep his secret.

Mydei shoves Phainon aside, striding in confidently into his home.

“...And to what do I owe this lovely crack of dawn visit?” Phainon drawls, rolling his eyes fondly and shutting the door behind him.

Mydei looks at him as if he should already know the answer, shrugging his bookstack up and down for emphasis. Then, he sets down his dusty tower of tomes on Phainon's dining table with a satisfied expression.

When Phainon remains bemusedly befuddled, Mydei says gruffly, “These are books on the Kremnoan language.”

Phainon's eyes widen, “Wait, you mean…”

Mydei crosses his arms, looks off to the side. If Phainon didn't know better, he'd say he looks slightly embarrassed. “You wanted to learn, didn't you?”

“That doesn't mean I want to study before the Waking Hour!!” Phainon complains, sitting down easily across from Mydei's bookstack from hell.

Mydei smirks back, pulling out his chair and settling into it. “Kremnoan warriors start their training before the Waking Hour is up. To learn our language properly, you should do the same.”

Phainon sighs, picking up the first book in the pile. He reads its title: A Dictionary and History of Insults in the Kremnoan Language. 

“You just wanted to see me suffer, didn't you.”

Mydei raises an eyebrow and all too gleefully repeats Phainon's last words before he left for the war on the black tide. “Who knows?”

Phainon glares at him, but turns to the first page without further complaint.

Mydei watches him expectantly. Not sure what said Mydei expects him to do, Phainon starts to read the first words in the dictionary and their translation to the common tongue. 

He reads about three increasingly colorful insults before he says, “...Is this really how you're going to teach me the language? Having me read the tomes you brought while you watch on silently?”

Mydei seems confused, unsure for a second. The expression is almost comical on a man of his dignity and stature, but Phainon valiantly reigns in his chuckle. 

“... I'm not sure,” he starts, serious, thoughtful, “I've never taught anyone my native tongue before. I'm a bit new to this.”

Phainon's heart does not melt into a puddle of goo, okay. His pulse is a very normal speed and he is very normal about this! “...You've really never tried to teach anyone else before?”

At this, Mydei crosses and then uncrosses his arms, before finally resting his clasped hands on the table. His gaze shifts down to his hands and then to the mountain of books he's brought to Phainon's home, before casting aside to the shadows. “...No one's ever wanted to learn before.”

Phainon drops the dictionary in his grip and reaches across the table to grasp Mydei's hands in his own. Not one day in his life will he allow Mydei to believe that his birth culture and way of life will destine him to be alone and shunned. His anger goes out to the people of Okhema, anyone who has told Mydei the words of his homeland are too coarse, too simple and blunt and brutal. 

His heart hurts at how eager Mydei was to start their lessons once Phainon confirmed his desire to learn. He thinks about how Mydei barged into his house not more than six hours after they left the pub, as if he needed to show up before Phainon could be fully awake enough to change his mind.

“...Mydei,” he says, carefully, slowly, waiting until Mydei’s gaze meets his own again. “I want to learn your language because I want to learn more about you. Your life, your homeland, everything that you are willing to share with me.”

Phainon squeezes Mydei's hands in his own. “Do you understand?”

Mydei nods, “I do.”

Phainon sits back in his seat, a small smile fitting his features. He hesitates over whether to pull his hands back—he's worried he's perhaps shown a bit too much of the heart on his sleeve. But ultimately, Phainon of Aedes Elysiae is a selfish man, and so he lets Mydei be the one to decide when to retract their hands.

…Though, Mydei does nothing of the sort? The only motion he makes is to start stroking his battle-calloused thumb up and down the back of Phainon's left hand.

He says, “Thank you, Phainon. I am no great teacher, but I will do my best.”

Phainon’s heart might actually beat out of his chest, squeezes his rib cage and leaves him breathless. “And I eagerly await your tutelage!” If his hands were not pre-occupied at the moment, Phainon would rub his right hand at the back of his neck. As it is, he makes do with a sheepish smile. “...Just, let's do it at normal waking hours, okay?”

“Okay,” Mydei smiles in return, and that's that.

Chapter End Notes

“Teacher,” Mydei says, standing imposingly in Anaxa’s doorway.

“Mydeimos,” Anaxa says, standing impatiently in Anaxa’s doorway. 

“How do I teach someone properly?” Mydei says, tone and figure braced for battle.

Anaxa sighs, gesturing to Mydei to come in. “...What are you trying to teach?”

Mydei sighs, too. “A language,” he admits reluctantly.

Anaxa rolls his visible eye. “What appears to be the issue? If Phainon is too … distracted when you try to teach him, just pull out a gun. Works for me every time when my students are daydreaming in class.”

Lady Aglaea, who Mydei pretends isn't in the middle of sneaking out of Anaxa's window for both of their sakes, says, “That's why your students hate you.”

Mydei frowns, crossing his arms. “I don't want him to hate me.”

Anaxa sighs, pouring a cup of coffee from the pot. Memories of Phainon casually ending Mydei's life fill his mind's eye. Well, better that than his sad pining expression when Mydei isn't looking, Anaxa supposes. “I don't think that's possible…”

Aglaea has since finished her clandestine exit and walks through the still open front door, shutting it behind her. “Since I was passing by, I'll help you figure out your problem, Mydeimos.”

Mydei is glad he’s been blessed since birth with a stoic face. “Okay.”

Anaxa pours a mug of coffee for Aglaea as well, and motions towards Mydei, “Tea?”

Mydei shakes his head, “That's alright, thanks.” He has a gut feeling it would be best if he leaves them to… whatever they were doing, as soon as possible. “So… how do I teach him?”

Anaxa sighs again, “Where are you hitting a barrier?”

Mydei says, “I don't really know what method to use.”

Anaxa sets down the coffee pot and seats himself back at the table. He considers. “Well, what's your lesson plan like? It could be a problem with the structure, I suppose.”

“Lesson plan?” Mydei asks, confused, “...Structure?”

Oh dear. “Learning a language is a task that takes consistent practice and reinforcement.” Anaxa adds two sugars to his own coffee and pours an entire cup of cream into Aglaea's. 

“It's also best to start with building vocabulary and then teach grammar after he has enough words under his belt to form simple sentences.”

Aglaea stands up poisedly, casually dumps her coffee into the sink, and pours a fresh black cup from the coffee pot.

Mydei's eye twitches, but he, ultimately, has surprisingly good self preservation instincts for an immortal being and wisely says nothing. “Does it matter which vocabulary I start with?”

“You probably should start with everyday phrases, common words in the vernacular.” Anaxa notes, sipping his coffee pointedly and sending Aglaea a side-eyed glance.

“Ah. Perhaps I wasn't too far off the mark, then,” Mydei muses consideringly, serious.

“How so?” says Aglaea, sipping her black-as-the-soul coffee with relish and throwing a side-eye back at Anaxa.

“I gave him a dictionary of Kremnoan insults, that's definitely everyday kind of language.” Mydei says, crossing his arms, feeling a bit proud of himself for his selection.

“I guess it probably is, for the two of you.” Anaxa sighs, long suffering. “But be sure to teach him other words too, for simple greetings and talking about your day and things like that.”

Mydei nods gravely, “Yes, that seems simple enough.” He pauses, considers, “But wait, how do I teach him new words? He thought it was odd that I gave him some books and waited as he read them.”

Lady Aglaea finishes her coffee and, horrifyingly, grabs another cup from the kitchen and starts on a second and third cup of coffee at the same time. “Try something more interactive. Perhaps explaining new word definitions and pronunciations, or how the translation applies in different contexts.”

Mydei nods again, sufficiently satisfied and scarred in equal measure by this encounter. “Noted. Thank you for your assistance, Lady Aglaea, Professor Anaxa.”

“Call me Anaxagoras.” Anaxa grumbles as Mydei makes his escape from the fresh hell that is Lady Aglaea and Anaxa living together in domestic bliss(?).

—

“Deliverer.” Mydei says, towering over Phainon's lunch, arms crossed and feet planted wide like he's ready for battle.

“Yes, Mydei?” Phainon says, a smile casting over his features and warming his expression on sight.

Mydei looks down at Phainon's sad lunch of bread and cheese and a disapproving frown appears on his face. “...You will eat my cooking for dinner instead of that poor excuse for a meal,” he says, gesturing to Phainon's plate.

Phainon's heart feels warm. "If you insist," He leans his head on his hand, resting his elbow on the table. His eyes soften. “then thank you, Mydei,” he says, sincere and soft.

Mydei sits down at the mess hall table across from him, satisfied. “Good. Also, meet me after Action Hour at my library.” His tone is flat but lifts up at the end, and Phainon knows him well enough to understand it's meant to be a question.

“I'll see you there after dinner, Guardian,” Phainon teases, a grin lifting his features. 

Mydei nods, “Yes, we will continue your language training then.” He gets up from the table and makes to leave from the dining hall. 

On the way out the door, Mydei looks back over his shoulder at Phainon. His eyes crinkle at the corners as he nods Phainon's way in acknowledgement.

...Somehow, he's picked up without being told that, after everything, all the loss and sacrifice, Phainon likes to be reassured that each meeting won't be the last.

Phainon feels his face start to burn, and he immediately returns to stuffing his face with bread as a distraction. If heart beats faster and louder, only he will know.

—

Mydei is already at that same nook in his library when Phainon enters. He realizes belatedly that this is likely Mydei's favorite getaway spot.

As his steps approach, Mydei looks up from the table, scattered with books and parchment and two quills. “Ah, Deliverer. Did you enjoy your dinner?”

Phainon grins, “It was delicious,” he sits down at the table across from Mydei as he bemoans, “I wish you'd cook for me more, I haven't had such a good meal in a long time!” 

Mydei nods, “I’m glad you enjoyed it. I'll cook for you again tomorrow, then.”

He says it like it's nothing, but Phainon's eyes begin to widen. “Really? I was just saying nonsense, you don't have to—”

Mydei levels Phainon with a look. “I would like to,” he says simply, then, a slight color tracing his cheek, he adds, “if that's okay.”

Phainon valiantly does not melt into his chair and says, soft, “...Yeah. It's definitely okay.”

Mydei claps his hands together. “Then it's settled. Now, take this.”

He hands Phainon a parchment filled with ink. Phainon looks it over briefly, recognizes it's all in Mydei's own handwriting. He made this for him? 

“I asked Anaxa for advice on how to teach you and he said I should start with explaining the basics,” Mydei says, pointing at the first word he wrote down, “This one, KMD, is pronounced ki-me-de , and means hello.”

Mydei knows that Phainon, despite what he'd have others believe, is in possession of a rather shrewd mind, and he picks things up quickly. So he's not surprised when Phainon says, hand to chin in thought, “So wait, this and HKS—and the words I read the other day in that insults dictionary, now I'm thinking about it—all are written with only consonants. Are all your words missing the vowels in-between when put in writing but not in speech?” 

“Yes,” Mydei says, eyes brightening the slightest bit, and Phainon notices how eager he is to talk about his homeland to a willing audience, “Our writing system is based in syllables, and a Kremnoan knows which vowels are implied by the consonants. It was a script adopted from Aquila’s sky kingdom after the Kremnoan conquest. Before that, we did not have a formal writing system of our own.”

Phainon nods, hand still at his chin. “How do you know which vowels accompany which syllables, then?”

Mydei leans back in his chair, thinking for a moment, “There are common syllabic patterns based on the order of the symbols. You'll pick it up with practice and learning more words.” He gestures to Phainon, “Try saying it: KMD.”

“Kiemed?” Phainon tries sounding it out but the syllables feel foreign on his tongue. But Phainon the Deliverer, Bearer of Worlds, is not someone who gives up so easily. Plus, there is no word for “giving up” in the Kremnoan language, he's almost certain. The thought makes him chuckle. “Ki-me-de,” he says, slowly. “ Ki -me-de. So, KMD?”

A satisfied smile crosses Mydei's expression, “Yes, that's not bad for your first attempt at Kremnoan pronunciation. Don't emphasize the first syllable though, there's no emphasis on any particular syllable in Kremnoan words.”

Phainon nods, “Got it. What about this next one?” he points to the next word (phrase? it has three words on the same line) on the list.

Mydei points to the word at the beginning of the phrase, written LKNM, “ Le-ke-in-im, which is a greeting. Roughly translated to the common tongue, it means nice to meet you.”

Mydei watches as Phainon traces the letters with his finger, mouth forming around the words silently, brows furrowed in concentration. He's taking this very seriously, as he always does when it comes to someone he cares about. The thought warms something deep in Mydei's chest. It's been a while since they could spend time together like this. He cherishes the moment.

Phainon's head jerks back up in triumph, “I think I've got it! LKNM! How was that?? Are you impressed with my Kremnoan yet?” he lilts, playful expression softening his eyes.

Sitting forward again in his chair and uncrossing his arms, Mydei says easily, “I am not surprised you are learning quickly. You pretend to be much less sharp than you are off the battlefield, but there's no need to do that with me.”

Somehow, the implication that Mydei sees him, really sees him, is just Not Good for Phainon's heart. He rests his pleasantly warm face on the cool stone of the tabletop, casts his gaze to the dusty bookshelves in embarrassment. “...I can't stand you, Mydei,” he whispers softly.

A sigh, and then Mydei flicks Phainon in the forehead. “Get up, HKS. Don't feel embarrassed over that. Your mind on and off the battlefield is something to be proud of.”

As Phainon sits back up, Mydei swears he hears him mutter something under his breath that sounds like, “...not what I was embarrassed about…” but since it's said quietly, and Mydei is unsure what he means by it, he doesn't reply. He also knows that if Phainon wanted a response, he would repeat it louder for Mydei to hear, so he doesn't put it to mind.

“Anyway!” Phainon says, brightening up as he returns to vertical orient, “Glad to see that the Kremnoan language really does have more than one word! What's the next one?”

Mydei points to the second word in the phrase after LKNM. “NMH,” he says, “Ne-mai-ha, it's pronounced. The word means name, and with the context of LKNM, it means ‘here is my name’, or ‘my name is’.”

“Ne-mai-ha, ne-mai-ha, ne-mai-ha,” Phainon says, enunciating each syllable carefully. “NMH?” he looks to Mydei for approval, who nods in response.

“Yes, that's right,” he says, pleased.

“I feel like I'm getting it! You know, for a first time teacher, you're really not so bad at this after all, Mydei,” Phainon says, grinning.

Mydei looks at the parchment between them on the table. “... I'm glad to hear that,” he says, sincere.

Phainon smiles back, even though Mydei can't currently see it with his gaze tilted downwards. “Let's keep going, what's the last word in that …sentence?”

Mydei looks up, gaze meeting Phainon's, before casting back down to the word he's written. Strangely, he hesitates for the first time in their study session, before saying, “Fai-no-ne, it's pronounced,” pointing at FNN on the page.” Another breath, then: “...that's your name, written in Kremnoan.” 

Mydei looks away after saying this, but Phainon can still see the pink tipping his ears. Kephale help him, this man is actually going to be the death of Phainon of Aedes Elysiae. Something about reading his name in Mydei's handwriting, the name he has given him in his native tongue, feels so intimate it hurts. 

Mydei seems to find the wall incredibly interesting for a moment, and Phainon is a bit struck dumb, tracing the syllables with his lips. Fai-no-ne. Fai-no-ne.

Phainon sits in a daze for a second before he sits up, determined. He says, slowly, softly, drawing Mydei's gaze, “KMD,” he waves at Mydei, “LKNM. NMH …FNN.” 

[Hello, it's nice to meet you. I'm Phainon.]

Mydei smiles, and it lights up his whole body, posture relaxed, open, kind. He waves back at Phainon, and the gesture should not be allowed to look cute on the Guardian of Amphoreous, what the hell. He reaches out a hand, as if to shake Phainon's in greeting, “LKNM, FNN. NMH MDMS.”

[Well met, Phainon. My name is Mydeimos.]

…MDMS, Mai-di-mos . Phainon feels like he should feel embarrassed and, well, he is—because it's Mydei and he's just a little bit madly in love with him so when is he not embarrassed—but mostly Phainon just feels… happy. How many people in the world still know that name, what must be his birth name bestowed by his mother? Phainon is honored to be trusted to hear it. He tucks the sound of that name in his heart for safekeeping.

In the end, one thing that's always been true about the two of them, is that, where one leads, the other follows. Phainon takes Mydei's outstretched hand, moves their hands together in rhythm, up and then down. 

It feels like a new beginning. And maybe it is—the start of their new lives. Not as the Deliverer and the Guardian of Amphoreous, but as simply Phainon and Mydei.

The thought makes him smile.

So! I based the Kremnoan language loosely on Linear B, a syllabic script from Mycenaean Greece, aka ancient Greek society ca. 1600-1100 BCE. And ofc based on the only in-universe canon word, HKS [pronounced in English canon as haikas].

Each syllable in Linear B is represented by a symbol, and it was adopted from the Linear A system for the most part from Crete after conquest by the Mycenaeans.

Speaking of…

Mycenaean culture is primarily known for its strong warrior tradition, its advanced architecture featuring citadels and palaces, and its influence on later Greek civilization through its language, art, and architecture. They were a dominant force in southern Greece during the Late Bronze Age, establishing fortified cities and engaging in trade and military campaigns.

The Mycenaean people were a warrior culture people, and I thought this fit Castrum Kremnos great so tada~

Everything is the same as before the end of the world. Phainon and Mydei spar, train, and take meals together. They compete over who can last longer in the hot baths, over who can help more people with reconstruction efforts, over who can eat the fastest, over who can best the other in arm wrestling.

…Mydei cooks him dinner, sometimes. 

Everything is the same, but it feels different. Something softer, kinder. More befitting a world that affords them the youth and frivolity destiny never allowed.

Another thing different from before, though, is that Phainon and Mydei study together in the library a few nights a week. Two blankets and pillows have found a home by Mydei's hand on their usual chairs in the nook, in anticipation for their late nights and brisk mornings. The casual consideration of the gesture makes Phainon's heart dance in his chest. 

Phainon hasn't studied this hard since the Grove, and even then, he only put in enough work to make sure he didn't get threatened with Anaxa’s gun. (An effort for naught in the end, but attempted nonetheless.) 

Mydei explains the culture of his words, tells Phainon tales of his people’s history, recounts moments of his life before he was Mydeimos the Undying, and Phainon never really liked studying back in school, not really, but he doesn't mind so much now. Not after everything. He's happy to tuck each day in the library away as a memory for his heart to keep. Somehow, this is a world where he gets to have Mydei sitting across from him, reading spectacles falling down his nose, smile etched in his eyes, all when he'd thought he lost him to their next lifetime. 

…It's nothing short of the happiest he's ever been in his life.

The days are peaceful, sitting in the library nook under the early eve’s starlight, speaking in hushed tones beneath shared blankets and passing pages of parchment back and forth in the candlelight. And now, after weeks and weeks of learning Kremnoan, Phainon feels like he's starting to get a deeper understanding of how the Kremnoan language works. It's highly visual, speaking with images and actions. A king is described by the word for responsibility, a warrior by the word for strength, water by the word for life.

…It's really a beautiful language, much like the person who speaks it. Phainon will never say that out loud, though. He quite likes what the two of them have. And if he has trouble concentrating when Mydei leans across the table in a rush to grab a tome he wants to show him, if his heart stutters when Mydei smiles with his whole heart, well, that's only for Aquila and her stars to know.

—

“Mydei!” Phainon calls, running to catch up to him on the streetpath, “I want our next lesson to be on Kremnoan words about feelings! Surely there must be some language to describe emotions, right?” 

Mydei tenses, hesitates. Though he does slow down to wait for Phainon to catch up, the action made reflexive through repetition across the years.

Phainon smirks, nudging his elbow to Mydei's ribs. “What’s that tense reaction for Mydei, are you nervous to talk about feeeeelings?”

“There is no word for ‘nervous’ in the Kremnoan language,” Mydei says, crossing his arms. Kings of Kremnos do not get nervous. Though to be fair, Mydei gave up kingship long ago.

“I'll take the topic into consideration for our lesson tonight,” he relents, after a moment.

Phainon pumps his fist in the air, “Yes!” He claps one hand to Mydei's non-armored shoulder, squeezes briefly. “I'm finally going to figure out if there really are no words for fear in your language Mydei, just you wait!” 

And with that, Phainon turns to run off again, hand held up in farewell. “See you tonight, then!” Phainon says, laughing and bounding away. Mydei is vaguely reminded of a chimera, and the thought brings a chuckle to his lips.

“See you tonight,” Mydei echoes, words hushed like a promise.

—

“Boy,” says Krateros, crossing his arms.

“Teacher,” replies Mydeimos, crossing his arms back.

Krateros takes in the sight of his pupil, noting the finger tap tap tapping on Mydeimos’ elbow. His gaze is cast far off into the distant mountains, and a light color grazes his cheekbones.

Sighing, Krateros says, “... It's something about that Elysiaen boy again, isn't it?” He pats the space next to him on the stone banister and Mydeimos sinks onto it, head falling to his hands.

“... He asked me to teach him words in the Kremnoan language for feelings,” Mydeimos says, grave.

“I…see,” Krateros says, although he does not. It's not natural to him, a born and raised Kremnoan, to speak of such things directly. 

After a moment, Krateros says, “Is it your own feelings you are hesitant to speak?”

“...I suppose so. If I teach him, he will understand.” There will be no shield by which to hide is left unsaid.

Krateros sighs again, the things he does for this child… “Is that a bad thing?”

Mydeimos looks up, puts a hand to his chin, says nothing for a while. Then: “... Could it not be?”

“Well, that depends on you,” Krateros says. 

“I see,” Mydeimos says. “Do you think it's alright for me to…” There are many ways he could finish that sentence, but he does not.

“Mydeimos,” Krateros says, leveling a hand on his pupil's shoulder. “You are king no longer. Take your choice in stride. The sun shines on this morning, and will set at Parting Hour, just as it did yesterday. We adapt with it.” The world is different than before, he doesn't say.

Mydeimos' expression does brighten then, something lifting in the corners of his eyes. “...You did not agree with my decision, before,” he says, almost amused.

“I would not have made it myself,” Krateros says, shaking his head slowly. “...That is precisely why you are the man our people needed.”

Mydeimos sits quietly for a moment, contemplates. Then: “Do you hate me for it? I changed our people's history in the course of a moment.”

Krateros puts a hand to his chin, considers. “The pride of our people is in our culture, our values.”

Mydeimos lifts his head, looks Krateros in the eye, watching, waiting for him to speak. He waits for a mountain to move.

“...You saved many lives that day, and after, including mine. At the expense of your own,” Krateros continues. “If there's anyone who most embodies Kremnoan honor and sacrifice, it's you, Mydeimos.”

Mydeimos’ expression does not change, and his arms do not uncross. However, the finger tap tap tapping at his elbow finally ceases. He nods, and something about his entire posture settles, sighs. “That's high praise indeed from you, master.”

“Hmph.” Krateros huffs. “Don't let it go to your head, boy.” 

A smile stretches across Mydeimos’ expression at last. “Wouldn't dream of it, master.”

The two of them sit together in silence for a moment, heads tilted towards times and lives of old. Eventually, the sun sets, and they part without a word.

—

For once, Phainon is the first to arrive at their corner of the library. He settles himself into the couch by the window, rests his feet lightly on the seat of the chair across from him.

He's set two mugs of tea in the table, brewed under a slow heat and then cooled with salted ice, in the Elysiaen style. Mydei had asked him about it the other day, over the dinner he had prepared for the two of them, so he's brought a second cup for him to taste.

Mydei shows up to their spot a few minutes later, scroll in hand and expression set. “I have decided to honor your request, Phainon.”

A grin lifts Phainon's lips in return, “Well then, don't keep me hanging, Mydei! I've been dying to know, you know.” He makes to move his feet off Mydei's usual chair, but Mydei waves him off, opting to sit adjacent to Phainon on the couch instead. In place of reacting to that, for the sake of his sanity, Phainon hands Mydei the tea wordlessly. Recovering, he teases, “Soooo, have you been lying to me about there not being words for emotions in the Kremnoan language, hmm?”

Mydei takes a sip, then sets down his scroll, tilting his head in thought. He doesn't hesitate, “No, but emotions in Kremnoan are…indirect. Highly dependent on context.”

Mydei gives the tea another sip, lips curving up in satisfaction. “...This is quite good.”

Color rises high to Phainon's cheeks, “It's nothing.” He raises his right hand to rub at the back of his neck. “Glad you like it.”

Mydei stretches out the scroll on the table, angling it to Phainon's view. He points to the first word on his list, and Phainon reads along the trace of his fingertips. “This is the word for home. It's said after battles snatched from the claws of defeat, when a comrade arrives to his family safe and uninjured. It is also used to describe small moments where a person's breath draws alongside another.”

Phainon's eyes settle at the corners, he says, softly. “...That’s how you describe joy, hmm?”

A nod, a smile. “Yes,” Mydei says, simply, sipping more of his tea. After a moment, he continues, pointing to the next word. “Here is the word for parting. It is used when a warrior falls, for the final farewell in this lifetime. I suppose in the common language you would call it sorrow.”

Phainon thinks of the expressions he cannot manage to hide around Mydei, of the day they bid each other goodbye for the sake of destiny and war chasing at their heels. He thinks of the tears he did not shed, he thinks of a ring retrieved from under the waves. “...I think I understand,” he says.

Mydei shifts closer so he can point out the next word further down the scroll. “There is no word or convention to describe fear, because Kremnoan culture traditionally did not believe in fear.” Mydei says, slowly, measured, “There is, however, a word for a person who is a coward. You could describe being afraid by calling yourself this.”

Phainon unconsciously leans forward again, until their hands touch, bare and gloveless, overlapping along the lengths of their pinkie fingers. “...How would you describe it?”

Mydie considers, taking a quill from Phainon's other outstretched hand. He writes two words with his hand bare and he does not falter. “This. Combining the words for known and change.”

Phainon smiles, aligns their fingers together slowly, palm to palm. “I think a little fear is a good thing. Makes us human, don't you think? That we care.”

Mydei takes their hands and folds them tight together. Simple, natural, like it's the way of the world. “I think so, too,” he says.

…Phainon is beginning to realize the way Mydei speaks in the common language reflects the nuances of his native tongue. He speaks in images, in stories, in actions that underlie emotions that words simply do not have the depth to describe.

After a beat, Phainon says, quiet, “You know, the Okhemans are absolutely wrong about your language and way of life. Your people are not unfeeling or cold. In fact, it’s rather the opposite, isn't it?”

Mydei nods, “We are unaccustomed to discussing emotions directly, but something unsaid is no less strongly felt.”

Phainon looks down at their hands, entwined together, like two spiders in love. He thinks of his own cowardice. The feelings he's left unsaid. “...I think I know what you mean.”

They sit for a while, trading silences. The stillness is only broken by the occasional sip from matching tea mugs. Something has changed. In them, in the world around them, in the future they built with their own hands.

If his mother were alive to see it, Mydei likes to think she would be proud of the home he holds to his heart. 
He doesn't let go.

In the space between teacups and twilight, Mydei is fearless.

Chapter End Notes

And there we have it, there really is no word for ‘fear’ in the Kremnoan language!

Romance, however……… 🤔

Sharing each other's silence is Mydei's love language and I will be stabbed in the tenth thoracic vertebrae on this hill, okay

It's nice, these days, to spend an afternoon in the baths not as a distraction from death and destruction and doom, but for the simple pleasure of easing into the evening.

Castorice sits to his right, head leaned on his shoulder, no longer dictated by curse or need to stay distant and detached. Hyacine is lounging with her eyes shaded, face tilted towards the sunlight, Tribbie is kicking her feet in the shallows.

“Snowy!” Tribbie is saying, drawing their attention. “I saw Aggy and Naxy eating dinner together yesterday!!!”

Phainon hums, tilting his head to rest on top of Castorice’s curls. “Were they arguing as always?”

Tribbie shakes their head. “Nope! Well, yes, they were arguing and shouting at each other like always, but they were alsoooo….” they pause for dramatic emphasis,”...holding hands!!”

Castorice looks up at Tribbie, says disbelievingly, “No way. The two of them?”

Giggling, Hyacine says, “Maybe it's not so hard to believe, is it? With her emotions back, Lady Aglaea is much more expressive than before.”

“Maybe it's some kind of competition?” Castorice muses, hand to her chin in thought.

“Nah, get this,” says Phainon, “Mydei told me he saw the two of them being all domestic at Anaxa's place a few weeks back. Soooooo,” he winks across the bath at Tribbie, “maybe it's a thing after all.”

“Hehe, maybe you're right,” says Hyacine, holding her hand up to cover her laughing lips.

Castorice nods, the movement almost a nuzzle in it's proximity, nudging Phainon's neck up and then down. “I suppose that does make sense, now I think about it. Lady Aglaea represents the Titan of romance, and Cerces and Mnestia were lovers, after all.”

“Speaking of romance!” Tribbie shouts excitedly, slightly startling Castorice with their volume. “How's it been going with De, Snowy?!”

Phainon flails, slipping off his seat in the bath and falling into the water, dislodging an amused Castorice. “WHAT. Wh-what are you saying, I'm not dating Mydei, what are you talking about??”

Tribbie tilts her head in innocent confusion, “You're not? But you go on all those library dates together!”

“D-dates?!” Phainon sputters, coughing up bathwater he inhaled in his hyperventilation frenzy. Castorice is vaguely concerned for a second he might pass out with how little he's breathing.

Hyacine giggles again, “And your spar and dinner dates too! You're really not subtle at all, Phainon!”

“...He's just teaching me Kremnoan, o-okay! Nothing like th-that at all!” Phainon protests, face turning red and eyes wildly darting around in mild panic.

Castorice has a mild smile on her face, which from her may as well be a full-body grin. “If you say so, Phainon.”

Phainon collapses back to his seat, head in his hands. “...They're not dates because he doesn't like me like that,” he says, a touch too quiet. Then, louder: “I'm just grateful he's taking the time to teach me. I wanna thank him somehow but I don't know how to say it? I've tried to tell him, but I… just can't get the words out, I guess.”

Hyacine says, thoughtful, “Have you tried writing it down, maybe in letter?”

Grateful for the shift in topic, Phainon says, half relieved, “... That's not a bad idea, actually.”

Tribbe adds brightly, “Ooh, you can write it in Kremnoan, so he knows for sure how much you care about what he's been teaching you!!”

…Could he write a letter to Mydei in Kremnoan? What would he even say? 

“What would I even say?” Phainon says.

“Thank him for taking the time to teach you,” Castorice says, simply.

“Tell him that you looooveee him!” Tribbie says, gleefully.

Phainon doesn't bother denying it. Not anymore, or maybe he never has. It's true, and likely anyone who's ever met him knows it. The sun shines bright, the sky is blue, and Phainon loves Mydei with all he has. These are just facts of the world.

“...I don't want him to see me differently,” Phainon says quietly, voice and face downcast.

“...Don't you?” says Hyacine, eyes kind. She's always been too perceptive.

“...What if I tell him and things become awkward?” Phainon whispers, looking down at his face reflected in the bathwater. He knows, deeply, that Mydei wouldn’t stop being his friend over his unrequited feelings. Mydei's not that kind of person, and if he was, Phainon wouldn't be friends with him, much less in love with everything he is and all that. But, Phainon's still terrified, that they'll be different, after he speaks his heart. That they'll lose their easy intimacy and affection to awkward aborted gestures and apologies.

“Take a page out of Mydei's book for this!” Tribbe says, moving her hands to her hips. Then, in a low gravelly voice made to imitate Mydei's baritone, “There is no word for ‘fear’ in the Kremnoan language!”

“There is for being a coward, apparently,” Phainon says, despairingly.

“How much scarier can it be telling De compared to saving the whole world?” Tribbie says, putting a hand to Phainon's left shoulder.

“Much more,” Phainon's voice cracks, voice quieting again, “...I fear my heart will break when he says no.”

“What if he doesn't?” Hyacine says. “Maybe he loves you, too.” 

“Me?” Phainon laughs deprecatingly, “That's impossible. I'm just the guy that follows him around challenging him to fights and competitions all the time.”

“You're also learning a whole language just to learn more about him. You're very observant regarding everyone you love, and you help ease our burdens.” Castorice says, sincere.

“There's a lot to love about you, Snowy!” Tribbe says, hands back on their hips and grin on their face.

…Phainon knew, on some abstract level, the way you know how the grass bends in the breeze below your feet, or the way the clouds billow in Aquila's sky, that his friends love him. But somehow, hearing it said out loud 

brings Phainon to tears. “Wow, way to make a guy feel appreciated…” he sniffles, wipes his nose.

Hyacine hugs him, wrapping her arms around his back, and Castorice hugs his left arm. “We do appreciate you in our lives,” Hyacine says, “And we know Mydei does too, regardless of whatever his answer will be.”

“Soooooo,” says Tribbie, excited, “Are you gonna tell him?!” 

Phainon laughs, ruffling the top of her hair with his only free hand, with Castorice and Hyacine clutching tight to his left and back. “...I'll think about it.”

—

A conversation on the rooftop:

Sometimes, they sit at the top of the world and look down, feet dangling off the city roofs. It's quiet up here, peaceful. A place they can see all the people who still yet breathe and live, all the people they sacrificed so much to protect.

Mydei and Phainon sit side by side, hands a breath apart. Phainon sighs, looking down and then away to the setting sun coloring the sky. 

Mydei says, still quiet so as not to bend the tranquil dusk, “What's up? Something's eating at you.”

Phainon sighs again. “...It's stupid,” he says, casting his eyes downwards.

“That's nothing new,” Mydei says, an amused gleam to his eyes.

Phainon shoves his shoulder beside him. “Shut up.”

After a second, Mydei says, gentle, “I meant it you know, when I said you can tell me anything.”

A third sigh. “...Okay, here goes.” A breath in. Then, “After everything, is it really okay for us to be like this?”

Mydei hums, leaning backwards and balancing his weight on his palms. “How do you mean?” 

Phainon leans backwards too, resting his weight on hands outstretched behind him. “I don't know… Happy? Not always fighting for everyone's lives?”

Mydei takes a moment, considers. When he takes time to think through something thoroughly, Mydei moves with his whole body, brow furrowing, finger tap tap tapping, weight shifting. Then: Mydei tilts his head and it falls a little closer to Phainon’s shoulder, just short of touching. “I think so,” he says at last, “After everything, we deserve a little joy and respite, don't we?”

Phainon can feel the heat of the airspace between them tingling at the back of his neck. Slowly, staying still as possible, as if to not alert Mydei to their proximity for fear it was an accident he will remedy if brought to awareness, Phainon says, “But what if it's not real? …What if it ends?”

Mydei pulls back a bit, and while Phainon can breathe a little easier, he misses the danger more than he should. Mydei says, looking Phainon in the eye, “Then we will rebuild.”

Phainon’s voice breaks as he says, “And? What if it ends, over and over again?”

Mydei nods, the motion made as if to move a mountain. “Then we will rebuild again and again.”

Phainon hums, swinging his legs back and forth. “You make it sound so simple,” he says.

“Is it not?” Mydei says, head tilted.

“...Being happy?” Phainon thinks about watching Mydei die over and over. He thinks about Trianne, about Anaxa, Castorice, Aglaea, Hyacine. He thinks about being the last one standing. “I don't know,” he says.

Mydei seems to accept this as an answer, nodding to himself. “Well, how about this,” Mydei starts, “Are you? Happy, I mean.”

Phainon looks over to Mydei, who shuffles closer to him and bumps their shoulders together softly. The act is so quietly affectionate it almost hurts.

Phainon really, really loves this man.

He tells no lie when he smiles and says, “I am. I'm very happy here with you.”

He bumps Mydei's shoulder back, and it leaves their hands almost touching.

Mydei folds their hands together. “And I, you.”

—

The former Chrysos Heirs try to take meals together when they can, enjoy the simple pleasures of cooking and eating together.

Aglaea and Anaxa are already sitting at a table in the mess hall, sitting on opposite sides and kicking each other under the table. Fairly civil for them, all things considered. Hyacine drags Mydei out from the kitchen to sit with them, and Lady Aglaea leads their prayer to Kephale for the harvest.

Hyacine is the first to speak as they dig into the meal. “Soooo, Mydei. Is there really no word for ‘romance’ in the Kremnoan language?” she starts innocently, “Because that sounds exactly like what you're doing with Phainon, hmm?”

Mydei is a great warrior and great warriors do not choke on their soup, so he does not choke. He just coughs a little in surprise, okay. “There is not…”

“But…?” Hyacine prompts, lips lifting her features knowingly.

Mydei sighs, looking from Anaxa's faux disinterested face, to Aglaea's look of please do not disappoint me Mydeimos, to Hyacine’s earnest expression. 

“...There is a word that describes love,” Mydei relents.

“And do you?” Lady Aglaea starts kindly, “Love him, I mean.”

Mydei's eyes widen in surprise, as if this even being a question confuses him. “Of course I do.”

Professor Anaxa speaks up for the first time in this conversation, apparently done playing disinterested. “You should tell him that.”
He grabs one of Aglaea's bread rolls and pops it into his mouth. 

Mydei's expression turns concerned for a moment. “...Does he not know?”

“Only way to find out is to ask, hmm?” Hyacine says kindly.

(Aglaea kicks Anaxa under the table, takes a large spoonful of his soup, and sips it all while making direct eye contact, which is as impressive as it is vaguely horrifying.)

…Mydei was under the impression that he was obvious with his feelings. He spars with Phainon most days, always seeks out his company, calls him his only equal, trusts him to have his back, and even is teaching him his goddamn native language, often while holding hands. 

He just assumed Phainon knew about his feelings. About how Mydei would shift time and space itself to make him smile. How he seeks Phainon's laugh the way the sun chases the moon.

But if Phainon doesn't know…? If he doesn't know what he means to Mydei…
Mydei needs to set that right.

He wants Phainon to know he is loved.

Chapter End Notes

So! In this good ending alternate universe future, the ‘flaws’ of each Chrysos heir have been removed, have been healed, so Castorice can touch people without it being the touch of death, Aglaea's emotions have returned, and Mydei is no longer cursed with immortality. Just a note.

We're close to the end now folks! Thanks for reading 💙

Clearly, this language is just as stubborn as Mydei himself!

But Phainon will find a way to be more stubborn and translate the letter he wrote if it fucking kills him, okay.

…The second thing he does is visit a library.

Mydei is on a mission. He sits down at the nook by the window, takes out a quill and scroll, ready for battle. He gets back up, drags his fingertips along the dusty banisters of the bookshelves as he looks for anything that would benefit his goal. 

After an hour of searching, Mydei sighs. Frustratingly, even his personal—and rather extensive—Kremnoan library has very little on the lost village of Aedes Elysiae. The only volumes he finds that mention the place are: a ledger of a merchant's sales, a journal of the wandering bard Archepia, and an old children's storybook that the bard brought back from the village.

Mydei settles back down into the chair in the nook, slides his glasses over his nose, and picks up the journal to read.

He learns that Aedes Elysiaens have a way with words, flowery and long winded, though perhaps exaggeratedly so when described by a foreign traveler. That Elysiaens take forever to waffle over decisions before making them, but, despite that, they are at heart a people of action, their actions made weightier by the convictions of their words. Mydei learns the Elysiaens have—or had, he supposes solemnly—a tight-knit community where every neighbor looked out for one another. Mydei's heart hurts for the people Phainon has loved and lost. 

Reaching the end of the journal, Mydei finds a few scraps of paper stuffed in the back cover. Taking them out to the morning light, he finds that the bard has included a couple recipes, too, for traditional celebratory foods from the town. He makes a mental note to try them out later. 

Mydei moves on curiously to the storybook. It, as the traveler described, is a simple tale. 

There once was a kind and courageous Prince who fell in love with a commoner. The Prince expressed his love for three days and three nights, unsuccessful with each passing Parting. His beloved turned him away each evening with scorn, disbelieving of the truth of his words. For, why would a Prince love a commoner?

On the fourth night, the prince brings his love a bouquet of flowers. He picks blossoms to match the color of his love's baby blue eyes, and he presents them with nary a word.

The fifth night, he brings his love's favorite foods, prepared and packaged neat and clean, and leaves them at the door.

On the sixth day, the Prince returns with a ring and a promise to cherish his love for all their days, if his words are accepted as true.

On the seventh day, the commoner arrives at the Prince’s castle, ring onhand, and weeps and weeps and weeps, for at last, his love is found true.

The bard has left a singular note at the backcover of the book binding:
This regales an old folk tale of Aedes Elysiae, based on Princes of ancient times. An older woman gave it to me, smiling, and told me to heed it well.

—

Phainon doesn't care much for picked flowers that wilt and die, Mydei knows. He prefers to let them grow in the wind, rather than be cut off at root. 

Mydei has a grand craftsman to see.

“...Chartonus,” Mydei says, grave. 

“Last King of Kremnos, what seek you?” Chartonus intones, looking up from his forge for a moment.

“I have a favor to ask of you…” Mydei begins.

—

Phainon sits with his head in his hands, wringing out his brain over a piece of parchment and three separate Kremnoan dictionaries.

Clearly, this language is just as stubborn as Mydei himself!

But Phainon will find a way to be more stubborn and translate the letter he wrote if it fucking kills him, okay.

Phainon refuses to be defeated by the Kremnoan language!

—

…Phainon has been thoroughly defeated by the Kremnoan language. After a couple days spent trying to find the right words, he's given up on translating the letter he wrote in the common tongue.

Phainon of Aedes Elysiae has no pride left to lose after his resounding defeat by a lexicon. Thus humbled, Phainon approaches a certain man, terror be damned. Let it not be said thus more that Phainon is a coward.

“...Krateros.” Phainon starts, wringing his hands nervously, “Thank you for meeting with me.” He itches to put one hand behind the back of his neck, but keeps his hands by his sides.

Krateros, sitting cross legged on the stonewall banister, raises an eyebrow. The gesture is reminiscent of Mydei's own mannerisms, and the thought makes Phainon smile, relax his shoulders a touch. The Kremnoan master says, stern and shrewd, “What do you want from me, child of the sun?”

Phainon takes a deep breath, then two, then four, and maybe he's actually hyperventilating?? 

…But then he stops, shoves a sheet of parchment at Krateros’ hand. In one breath he says, “HowdoIsayIloveyouinKremnoan.”

Krateros looks Phainon up and down. And then up and down again. It feels like he's being assessed for something. Phainon tries valiantly not to squirm under the scrutiny. “So,” Krateros says finally, crossing his arms, “you've finally got the balls to court Mydeimos.”

Phainon turns pink, hand finding the back of his neck, “...Yes?”

“Do you think I'll approve of you, son?” Krateros uncrosses his arms, just to recross them again. If it's an intimidation tactic, it's very effective, in Phainon's opinion!

(Phainon sometimes forgets that, after his mother's death, Krateros is the closest thing to a parent that Mydei has. He's glad they have each other. It means a lot to have family, Phainon knows better than most.)

However, Phainon is low-key terrified, actually, now he thinks about it, that Mydei's father figure won't approve of him and his confession. But Phainon did not save the entire fucking world just to die a HKS, or whatever. He steels his shoulders and looks Krateros direct in the eye. “Sir, I have protected his back in battle more times than I can count. We describe each other as our only equal on the battlefield. I have loved him throughout every time and space I've crossed and I survived Era Nova to come back to him. Is that not proof enough?”

Krateros stays stern, cold, arms still crossed, expression unyielding. Then, he uncrosses his arms, and he does not recross them. A hearty grin breaks out on his face. “...You will do.” 

He grabs for the paper and quill still resting in Phainon's arms. “I'll write down the translation for you.”

Phainon smiles too, relieved. He says, solemn, serious, hand to his heart in a bow, “Thank you for your blessing, Master Krateros.”

Krateros finishes writing down the translation, and hands him the parchment with a clap on his shoulder that nearly bowls Phainon over in its force. 

“Go get him, son,” he says.

—

“Is it doneeeee yet, De??” Tribbie whines, impatient. They're sitting at the kitchen counter, watching as Mydei spins spoons and spatulas in pots and pans. 

“Almost,” Mydei says, adding a pinch, then two, three, of herbs to his mixture, standing guard as the broth boils and simmers.

“I couldn't care less about this,” Anaxa says, sitting at the counter beside Tribbie, utensils in hand and poised to taste.

“Sure you don't, Naxy,” Tribbe says, gleeful, hands on their hips and rolling their eyes.

“I don't, and unlike you I am patient too,” Anaxa says, impatient.

Mydei puts a pot lid over his soup, hefts the pot over to two bowls, pouring a generous portion into each. “Well, regardless you won't have to wait any longer. Here,” he says, placing the bowls in front of Tribbe and Anaxa, “try this.” He's not nervous, per se, but Mydei does feel a certain tension in his shoulders, waiting, anticipating. He hopes this recipe is good.

Tribbie tries to eat it immediately, burning their finger on the copper spoonhandle. “Ouchie, it's hot still!” they put their spoon down, glaring at it in mild betrayal.

“Hmph,” Anaxa says, waiting for a minute and then blowing on his spoonful until it's a palatable temperature. “That's what happens when you take too much haste, Tribbie.” He takes a graceful sip from the soupspoon, then sets it down.

Tribbie blows and huffs at her spoonful and takes a sip too, “That's really yummy, De!” they grin.

“...It's not bad, actually,” Anaxa says, taking another spoonful. “I think this dish will do fine,” he says, nodding. He's also manifested ice and a bandage from somewhere(?) and is wrapping it around Tribbie's finger along the burn lines.

Mydei's shoulders relax, settling. “I'm glad,” he says. A smile lines his lips, it's nice to see their old teacher cares so deeply about them all, but he also knows better than to confront him about it.

“And your thoughts, Tribbie?” Mydei asks, once Tribbie's burn has been treated.

“This one is just as good as the other three you had us try, mhm!” Tribbie grins. Mydei is glad they liked the dishes, but that doesn't help him narrow down the options…

“This is a better choice than the cake you made I believe,” Anaxa adds, hand to chin in thought. “Better something sturdy and substantial in romantic affairs, and this will do very nicely.”

Mydei nods. He is vaguely horrified thinking about what Anaxa’s idea of romantic affairs constitutes, but he wisely stays silent.

—

It's as they're putting away their practice blades in the training grounds' weapon house that Mydei says, “...Tomorrow is the anniversary of the day we first met.” 

Phainon starts to feel his face flush, returning his blade to rest next to Mydei's on the spear rack. “...You remember that?” he asks, voice soft.

Mydei looks at him, a small frown forming on his face. “...Do you not?”

Phainon smiles, shoves Mydei's shoulder playfully as they exit the weapon house to the city-streets. “Of course I do, it's important to me,” he says, eyes dancing.

Mydei nods, satisfied. He bumps Phainon's shoulders back. “It is to me too, MKN.”

“Are you ever going to tell me what that means??” Phainon complains, burying his head into Mydei's shoulder as they walk.

Mydei says, smug, “...Maybe.”

“So, mysterious! I'll let you keep your secrets, for now.” He lifts his head up from Mydei's shoulder, an idea seeming to come to him. “About tomorrow! We should have a toast and celebrate the old times,” Phainon says, calm, collected, casual, heart not at all about to beat out of his chest, okay.

Mydei nods in agreement, hand casually wrapping around Phainon's left. “Yes, that was what I was going to ask you. The roof at Parting Hour?”

Phainon grins back. “As always,” he says.

…Tomorrow, he’ll be ready. But for today, Phainon basks in the warmth of Mydei's smile and he doesn't let go of his hand.

—

A conversation on the rooftop:

At early twilight, Phainon arrives to their vantage point at the top of the world, finding it complete with a table set with candles, soup, and sword. 

“Mydei, what? This is…” He trails off, breathless.

“I read about Aedes Elysiae. There was a traveling bard's journal in my library,” Mydei says, gesturing for Phainon to take a seat. “This soup recipe was in that journal, so I did my best to reproduce it. Tribbie and Professor Anaxa both confirmed its taste, so I hope it's to your liking even if it's not an exact recreation.”

Phainon takes a seat, stunned. In front of him is not an exact match, but the smell is so akin to the soup his mother used to make, he feels tears start to form in his eyes. “Mydei,” he says, soft, “...thank you.”

…There's no way Mydei understands the implications, right?? Right??

This must be some bizarre fantasy and Phainon is hallucinating?? It's either that, or… Phainon can't finish the thought, heart in his throat.

Mydei nods, looks Phainon in the eye as he says, sincere, “I wanted to show you the same devotion you showed me.” Mydei's entire being softens. “...I hope I did it justice.”

Phainon rests his face to the stone tabletop, cheeks burning against the cool surface. “...It's everything I could have asked for,” he whispers.

Mydei nods, satisfied. “Good,” he says, simply.

From his vantage point with face to table, Phainon has a close-up view of the sword resting on the stonetop. He sits up slowly, taking the blade in hand and looking wonderingly over its craftsmanship. Petals of morning glories are engraved within the bladework, pommel adorned on one side with a sun, and the other the moon. “This is… beautiful,” he says, awestruck.

Mydei nods, “I know you do not like flowers, so I commissioned this instead as a substitute. Chartonus forged it for me according to the design I requested.” Mydei puts a hand to his cheek, supported by his elbow on the table. A smile lifts the corners of his lips. He says, soft and sincere, "This blade will protect you whenever I cannot.”

Phainon feels his eyes start to threaten tears. “Mydei…”

“...And,” says Mydei, pulling out something from under the table and taking Phainon's hand in his own. “I would like you to have this.”

He drops something cool and metallic into Phainon's hand? Phainon looks, and it's… it's??

“I can't possibly accept this!” Phainon's eyes widen in disbelief. “This is your mother's ring.”

Mydei nods. “It is. I want you to have it.”

Phainon stares, dumbstruck. “I- really? Me?”

Mydei sighs affectionately, “Who else, MKN?” He looks down at the table between them, where Phainon's hands have folded instinctively over the ring. The gesture warms something in his chest.

Mydei’s free hand tap tap taps on the table. He thinks of the storybook, of the way the Prince's lover doubted at first the depth of his affections. “...Do you believe me?” he says, voice gentle.

Tears begin to fall and fall and fall. Phainon says, soft, “...I do.”

Mydei smiles at that. Good. That's what matters the most. That Phainon understands how cherished he is. But, there is one more thing he wants to know. “And…” Mydei starts, slow, steady, “...your answer?”

Phainon's own lips soften to a smile, eyes dancing to the music of the candlelight. “I have something for you, too.”

He pulls out from his cloak a piece of parchment, and hands it to Mydei.

You are my every day. It reads, in Kremnoan.

“I asked Krateros for help,” Phainon says, quickly, embarrassed, hand coming up to rest at the back of his neck. “...I hope you like it?”

Mydei's lips lift, he has chosen well the man to be his equal. Teasing, he says, “You know, there is no word for ‘romance’ in the Kremnoan language.”

Phainon squawks, faltering for a second, “W-wait, did I read this entirely wrong???” his face flushes even deeper red, “Oh Titans, I'm so sorry–”

“No, no,” Mydei smiles, indulgent. “I was only saying there is a word that describes love.”

“...huh?” Phainon says, confused. “ But I translated what Krateros wrote to mean ‘every day’?”

Mydei nods, “It does. The literal translation means, I will be with you every day. I would translate it to the common tongue to mean: I love you in every moment, through everything I do, each day we draw breath.”

Phainon collapses to the table, faceplanted to the stonetop. “Mydei,” he says, “I am so serious when I say I'm madly in love with you.”

Mydei crosses from his side of the table to Phainon’s and gathers him in his arms, hands coming to rest over his heart. “Good,” he says, a satisfied smile gracing his lips. “And I, you, MKN.”

Phainon looks up from Mydei's lap. He laughs and laughs and laughs, eyes bright and warm and so very alive. 

A moment later, when he's recovered from being a puddle in Mydei's arms, Phainon says, “Come to think of it, you've used that word to describe me before, but you never told me what it means.”

For the first time tonight, Mydei blushes, though he does not look away. “The literal translation is ‘someone who is an equal’. But perhaps a more accurate translation is, someone who is the pair of your soul.”

Phainon sits up quickly, almost knocking his skull into Mydei's in his haste. “Mydei,” he says, grave. “I want to kiss you so bad. Can I–”

Before he can finish his sentence, Mydei leans in and fits their lips together. 

After all, in Kremnoan, actions speak louder than words.

—

Fin.

—

Some time later:

“...And then, his dramatic ass made me a dish from my homeland, and got me a fucking sword ‘to protect me whenever he could not’ and gave me his mother's ring!” Phainon complains, smashing his ale cup to the pub table, liquid sloshing out the edges. “I can't stand him! How could he do this to me??”

Castorice says, indulgent, “We know, Phainon. This is the third time you've told us this story already.”

Anaxa adds, “And we were the unwilling test subjects for his Elysiaen cooking attempts.” 

Aglaea raises a disbelieving eyebrow daintily, “...Unwilling, hmm?”

Tribbie says gleefully, “I didn't know De was such a romantic!”

Phainon plants his face into the table, groaning in defeat. “I just love him so much, why is he like this…”

Mydei himself just sits with his hand in Phainon's, looking rather pleased with himself. “Aw, you love me, Deliverer?”

Phainon, face still kissing the tabletop, raises the hand not in Mydei's into the air and swats it back and forth as if to smack him, “Shut up, MKN.”

“...MKN?” Anaxa starts, head tilted in confusion. He has no drink of his own, but no one is fooled with Anaxa drinking from Aglaea's ‘second glass’, which ‘happens’ to be Anaxa's favorite wine.

“It's one of the most romantic words in the Kremnoan language!” Phainon complains, ungluing his face from the table. “It means soulmate.” He says, proudly.  

“Wait!” Tribbie says, hand covering their mouth in surprise, “That's the word Mydei says all the time about Phainon!!” Tribbie laughs, delighted. “I knew it didn't mean ‘loser’!”

“Shut up and drink your grape juice,” Mydei grumbles.

Hyacine giggles, hiding her mirth beneath her palm. It's really lovely to get to share this time with everyone. That, here and now, they love with all the time in the world.

Chapter End Notes

And that's a wrap, consider your yaoi undoomed!
